digest.title:
LP Mastermind
Market Update
digest.subtitle: What moved this week, what it means for your ranges, and what's worth talking about.

snapshot.label: Volatility
snapshot.value: Steady on the day, noisy macro backdrop

digest.intro: Bitcoin quietly closed out its best month since 2017 even with fresh Iran strikes and a hawkish Fed in the headlines this week. This issue touches almost the whole toolkit -- Range and Market Sentiment, Volume and Average Volume, Correlation, and Asset Selection -- across five very different stories.

stories.title: Bitcoin's Best Month Since 2017, With Real Noise Underneath
stories.body: Bitcoin held above $78,000 this week even as fresh US strikes on Iran rattled stocks and pushed oil prices higher, and a hawkish Federal Reserve kept rate-cut hopes in check. Despite all that, Bitcoin is on track for its best month since 2017. That combination -- calm price action sitting on top of real geopolitical and macro noise -- is exactly the setup where Range width matters most. A narrow range would have captured strong fees while price stayed put, but any Fed surprise or escalation headline could still knock a tight position out of range fast. The Coin Market Cap Fear and Greed gauge is worth checking too: a month this strong tends to push sentiment toward greed, and extreme greed has historically been closer to a correction than a continuation. If the gauge is creeping toward extreme greed, that's worth weighing before setting your range any wider toward the upside.
stories.spark: Where does the Fear and Greed gauge sit right now, and has that changed how wide you're setting your ranges this week?

stories.title: Hyperliquid's Path Onshore Could Mean New On-Chain Volume
stories.body: Hyperliquid, one of the largest on-chain perpetual futures exchanges, is reportedly in talks with Kraken's parent company Payward to route its perpetuals trading through Payward's US-regulated exchange, Bitnomial -- Hyperliquid's first real path into the US market. Former SEC and CFTC officials are separately pushing regulators to take a lighter touch on crypto derivatives so more of this trading can move onshore. If that deal closes, a slice of perpetuals volume that currently trades offshore could start flowing through US-accessible venues, and some of that activity tends to spill into spot swaps and on-chain pools as traders hedge and rebalance. Keep Average Volume (45-day) in mind before chasing any pool that lights up around this news. Krystal only shows today's volume, so a launch-week spike in a Hyperliquid-related pool can look like a huge APR opportunity. Pulling the 45-day average first tells you whether that spike is a new normal or just noise that reverts once the headlines fade.
stories.spark: If a Hyperliquid-related pool shows a huge APR this week, what would you check before adding liquidity -- and has checking the 45-day average ever changed your mind on a pool that looked too good?

stories.title: Strive's Bitcoin Treasury Keeps Growing
stories.body: Strive just added 1,800 Bitcoin and became the fifth-largest public company holding Bitcoin on its balance sheet. TD Cowen now expects Strive to end 2026 with 27,156 BTC, nearly 4,300 more than the firm previously forecast. That's another company committing to sustained, large-scale Bitcoin buying, layered on top of buying we've already seen from other treasury companies this year. When you see this kind of sustained buying, keep in mind there are two different levers, and they're alternatives, not additions. One is a correlated pair -- two assets that move together, like BTC and ETH. If you believe Bitcoin keeps climbing and expect Ethereum to move with it, a correlated pair lets both sides of your pool rise together, so you capture the full move instead of only half of it. The other is skewing your range -- setting more of your range above the current price if you expect Bitcoin to keep climbing, which gives you more exposure to the upside within whatever pair you're already in. Pulling both levers only makes sense if you hold a more specific view, like believing Bitcoin keeps climbing AND that it outperforms ETH along the way -- that's a bigger bet to commit to.
stories.spark: Given the pace of treasury buying this year, are you leaning toward a correlated pair, a skewed range, or neither right now -- and why?

stories.title: XRP ETFs Hit Nine Straight Days of Inflows
stories.body: Spot XRP ETFs have pulled in money for nine straight days, adding up to $1.6 billion in net inflows since launch -- even as XRP's price has cooled off during that stretch. Steady, one-direction buying like this is the classic setup for thinking about Range. If you're running an XRP pair and believe the buying pressure continues even though price has cooled, skewing your range higher gives you more room to capture the move if it resumes. The non-obvious second variable here is Correlation. If you want fuller exposure to a renewed XRP move rather than half of it, an XRP pair against an asset that tends to move the same direction as XRP captures more of the upside than an XRP/USDC pair, where the stable side sitting still cuts your gains in half.
stories.spark: With nine straight days of inflows but price cooling, do you read that as XRP about to catch up to the buying, or as buying pressure fading -- and how would that change your range?

stories.title: Sberbank's $46 Billion in Crypto Trading, and Its Choice of Assets
stories.body: Russia's Sberbank says it's already seeing $46 billion in crypto trading volume, and a deputy chairman told state media that figure could reach 4 trillion rubles in its first year. The bank is also preparing to offer loans backed by Ethereum and USDT once regulators sign off. It's worth noticing which assets a major bank chose for its lending product. Sberbank didn't pick some obscure token -- it picked Ethereum, a top-5 asset by market cap, and USDT, the largest stablecoin, the same market-cap-rank thinking behind Asset Selection playing out at bank scale. The other side of this is Volume. $46 billion in trading activity from a single bank is a large number, and if any share of that starts touching on-chain markets as the lending product rolls out, that's added swap activity moving through Ethereum and stablecoin pools -- more volume relative to TVL is what pushes APR up, so this is worth watching as a potential tailwind for ETH and USDT pairs down the line, even if it hasn't shown up yet.
stories.spark: If Sberbank's ETH and USDT-backed loans go live, would you expect that volume to show up in the pools you're watching -- and how would you tell the difference between a real shift and a short-lived spike?

digest.closing: What are you watching going into next week? Drop your current setups, pairs, and range thoughts in the group.
